title: Monorepo Strategies
description: Structure and manage large-scale monorepos with Git submodules, subtree merges, and tooling that keeps builds fast.

data.text: A monorepo stores multiple related projects in a single repository. When done well, it simplifies dependency management and cross-project refactoring. When done poorly, it bloats clone times and obscures ownership. Advanced Git tooling can help you get the benefits without the pain.

Monorepos shine when teams need atomic commits across services, shared libraries, or coordinated releases. You can refactor an API contract and every consumer in the same pull request, avoiding the integration lag that plagues multi-repo setups.

Submodules let you embed one repository inside another at a specific commit. They are useful when a project genuinely needs an external dependency tracked by Git rather than a package registry. The trade-off is extra complexity: developers must initialize and update submodules explicitly.

data.title: Add and update a submodule
data.code:
git submodule add https://github.com/example/lib.git external/lib
git submodule update --init --recursive

# After cloning a repo with submodules
git clone https://github.com/example/monorepo.git
cd monorepo
git submodule update --init --recursive

data.text: Subtree merges copy another repository's contents into a subdirectory of your repo while preserving its history. Unlike submodules, there is no separate working directory or extra clone steps. This makes subtrees simpler for small-to-medium shared code.

data.title: Add a repository as a subtree
data.code:
git remote add -f shared-lib https://github.com/example/lib.git
git subtree add --prefix=libs/shared-lib shared-lib main --squash

data.title: Use subtrees for small shared libraries
data.text: Submodules shine when the embedded repo is large, independently versioned, and rarely changes. For smaller libraries that need frequent joint refactoring, subtrees reduce cognitive overhead.

For extremely large monorepos, Git supports partial clone and sparse checkout to avoid downloading every file. These features let developers work on a subset of the tree while still using standard Git commands.

data.title: Sparse checkout for a single service
data.code:
git clone --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/example/monorepo.git
cd monorepo
git sparse-checkout set services/payments

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Monorepos simplify cross-project refactoring but can bloat clone times.
Use submodules when embedding external, versioned dependencies.
Use subtree merges for simpler shared-library workflows.
Partial clone and sparse checkout keep large monorepos usable.
